citations.quote: MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers have deferred approval of the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), in a bid to summon and force Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to address violence and child safety concerns on Facebook.
At Wednesday’s plenary deliberations, the House suspended the DICT’s 2027 budget as they wanted Zuckerberg to face the agency during an inquiry into social media safety.
The House of Representatives late Wednesday deferred deliberations on DICT proposed 2027 budget due to online safety issues.

MANILA, Philippines – The House of Representatives late Wednesday held off from further discussing the Department of Information and Communications Technology’s (DICT) proposed 2027 budget, as lawmakers flagged online safety concerns during floor debates on the agency’s spending plan.

Philreca party-list Rep. Presley de Jesus motioned that debates on DICT’s P10.68 billion be deferred as lawmakers would rather await the results of its efforts to curb harmful online content, crack down on scams and secure agreements with social media platforms.
Add to that a lingering concern over online scams, and the situation has brewed mounting frustration among lawmakers that ultimately prompted them to put on hold the DICT’s budget.

The House of Representatives deferred the consideration of the proposed budget of the DICT and its attached agencies following an interpellation concerning online safety, digital scams, and platform accountability.

The development comes as the House of Representatives deferred the consideration of the proposed budget of the DICT and its attached agencies following an interpellation concerning online safety, digital scams, and platform accountability.

Citing the lack of visible, immediate results in curbing scams and protecting minors, De Jesus moved to defer the budget deliberations, a motion that was supported by the majority and formally approved by the leadership.
The House majority bloc supported de Jesus’ motion to shelve DICT’s budget debates with no objections.
